subject: SOC 2: SDLC artifact handover and credential flow clarifications
messages:
From: Alice Harper <alice.harper@northridge-security.com>
To: camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Cho <ben.cho@acmebank.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 evidence: credential issuance and CI/CD gating - initial ask

Camila,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of the SOC 2 review for Acme Bank we need a concise package showing how Redwood manages: code review enforcement, CI/CD gating for production deploys, secrets/credential issuance and rotation, and the change ticket trace to deploy. Specifically we want:

- A short narrative of the credential lifecycle (who can request, approval flow, issuance, rotation cadence).
- CI job definitions or pipeline snippets that demonstrate gating (fail fast, required checks).
- A mapping between change tickets and deployed release hashes for a recent production rollout (June 2028 preferred).
- The PR approval matrix and any exceptions (e.g., emergency patch flow).

If you can attach a redacted sample (no live credentials) and point to any Drive or DocuSign links for attestations, that would be great. We have a narrow window this week — can you confirm ETA?

Thanks,

Alice Harper
Senior Assessor
Northridge Security

--
Attachment: request-checklist-soc2.txt (text)
From: camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Harper <alice.harper@northridge-security.com>
Cc: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence: credential issuance and CI/CD gating - initial ask

Alice —

Appreciate the clear list. I've pulled together a compact bundle and included a short narrative below; full artifacts are attached and a Drive link is included for the verifier package. High-level summary first, then the attachments.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Credential lifecycle: request via internal portal (confluence -> request form) -> approval by manager + security reviewer -> ephemeral token minted by KMS/STS for CI runners (default TTL = 1 hour) -> automated rotation every 24 hours for service accounts, immediate rotation on key compromise.
- Secrets management: we use a centralized KMS (customer-managed KMS optional for Private installs), secrets are never stored in repo. CI injects secrets at runtime via transient vault tokens; logs redact secret material.
- CI/CD gating: pipelines require green unit, integration, and static analysis; PRs require 2 reviewers for services owning prod traffic; security scans run as mandatory checks.
- Change traceability: each deploy references a Jira change ticket (see mapping sheet) and the CI pipeline records the deploy artifact SHA and timestamp to the release ledger (attached).

What I'm attaching (redacted):
- sdlc-credential-flow-v1.2.pdf — narrative + diagram of request -> approval -> issuance and rotation.
- ci-pipeline-gates.yaml — sanitized pipeline showing required gates and mandatory checks.
- pr-approval-matrix.csv — who can approve which area and required review counts.
- change-ticket-mapping-2028-06.xlsx — mapping for the June 14 deploy (artifact SHAs and ticket IDs).

Notes and caveats:
- The artifacts are redacted of token values and internal IPs. If you need original logs for sampling we can provide a secure viewer session; let me know who will access and we'll create a time-bound link.
- Emergency patches follow the documented exception flow (section 3 of sdlc-credential-flow-v1.2.pdf) and require after-the-fact attestation by engineering + security.

ETA: I can share these attachments now (attached) and provide a brief walk-through call tomorrow morning (2028-07-01 09:00 PT) if that works for your team.

Regards,

Camila Reyes
Manager, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: sdlc-credential-flow-v1.2.pdf (pdf); ci-pipeline-gates.yaml (yaml); pr-approval-matrix.csv (csv); change-ticket-mapping-2028-06.xlsx (xlsx)
Drive package: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/s/sdlc-credential-flow-v1.2

Date: 2028-07-01T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence: credential issuance and CI/CD gating - initial ask

Camila / Alice —

Quick technical clarification to supplement Camila's package:

- CI gating: the pipeline enforces checks via platform-enforced required statuses. Examples: unit-tests (pytest), infra-lint (tflint), static analysis (semgrep), and SBOM generation. The pipeline step names are the canonical gate markers; any missing marker fails the merge block. See the attached ci-pipeline-gates.yaml for the exact step names.

- Token issuance: ephemeral tokens are issued by the token service (STS) with the following flow: request -> manager-approved grant -> token minted with role-limited permissions -> token returned to runner only in-memory. No tokens are written to disk.

- Evidence note: for the June 14 release the CI audit log shows token issuer IDs and deploy SHA; we've redacted the token strings but can share a time-bound, read-only log export for Alice. Link to the Jira change is JIRA: INF-4521.

If the assessor needs samples of the audit export, tell me who and I'll stage a secure viewer.

Jordan Blake
Senior Software Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference

Camila / Jordan —

Received the package, thank you. The narrative and the sanitized artifacts look good and address most of our questions. A couple of follow-ups before we close the control: 

1) Can you provide a signed attestation (DocuSign or equivalent) from your security lead confirming the emergency patch exception flow and that the after-action attestation process is enforced?
2) We reviewed the change-ticket mapping and need the earliest creation timestamps for the transient tokens used during the June 14 deploy (redacted strings ok, but timestamps and token IDs required).

If you can stage a read-only log export for the token issuance events (time-bound link) and the signed attestation, we should be able to finalize this control.

We can take the log export through a secure viewer; please send the viewer link and the reviewer list (names and emails) so we can confirm access.

Thanks again — I'll stand by for the viewer link and the signed attestation.

Alice Harper
Senior Assessor
Northridge Security
